question: Is Central line noise damaging passengers' hearing between Liverpool Street and Mile End?
norm_question: is central line noise damaging passengers hearing between liverpool street and mile end

answer.text: The evidence cannot show whether noise between Liverpool Street and Mile End damages passengers' hearing, as TfL's 82 to 87 dB LAeq figures are in-cab measurements and our 87.3 and 91.9 dB(A) saloon app readings are indicative single-trip measurements.

verified_claims.text: The retrieved documents and our measurements cannot show whether Central line noise between Liverpool Street and Mile End is damaging passengers' hearing, because workplace exposure action values apply to workers and neither source assesses passenger hearing outcomes.

In FOI-1231-2425, TfL reported Central line measurements taken within the train operator's cab on 24 June 2024 of 87 dB LAeq eastbound and 86 dB LAeq westbound between Liverpool Street and Bethnal Green, and 83 dB LAeq eastbound and 82 dB LAeq westbound between Bethnal Green and Mile End.

citations.quote: these measurements were taken from within the train operator's cab

verified_claims.text: Our indicative NIOSH sound level meter app recordings in the passenger saloon measured whole-trip LAeq levels of 91.9 dB(A) eastbound and 87.3 dB(A) westbound between Liverpool Street and Mile End across 1 trip per direction including platform and dwell time, using an iPhone microphone validated only up to about 85 dB(A).

In FOI-2986-2324 (published 12 December 2023), TfL Case Officer Eva Hextall stated that TfL did not have a study on in-carriage Tube noise on the London Underground at that moment, while in a 9 December 2022 letter TfL's Head of Track Duncan Weir described noise exposure training and hearing tests specifically for Train Operators.

citations.quote: We don't have a study on in-carriage Tube noise on the London Underground at the moment.
General noise awareness training should be provided to Train Operators, which includes information regarding their daily personal noise exposure
should receive regular hearing tests as part of a health surveillance programme
